input.prompt: A dramatic hero shot, camera high and looking down at about 50 degrees, onto a dense green motherboard. Four identical long rectangular chip packages, each exactly 2.5 times as long as it is wide, lie in four parallel sockets side by side in a column, front to back, filling the frame: their top faces are completely FLAT, plain, matte light grey, perfectly blank rectangles with crisp edges and gold pins along both long sides. The FRONT (nearest, lowest in the frame) socket is gold-plated; its chip is lifted a little out of it, floating on a column of warm golden light pouring up from the gold socket, casting gold light on everything; the other three chips sit flat in dark steel sockets behind it. Beside each socket, on its right, a small empty dark smoked-glass display window in a gold bezel, unlit. Painted American comic book art of real computer hardware, in exactly the style of the reference images: one warm golden key light, a thin green rim light on the left edges and a red rim light on the right edges, bold ink contour lines, rich painted metal, dense realistic printed-circuit-board detail, black void background. Palette: black, deep PCB green, red, gold. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no symbols.
